name: Poha
cuisine: Maharashtrian (Mumbai-style kanda poha), also eaten across Madhya Pradesh and Gujarat

ingredients.name: Groundnut oil (or any neutral cooking oil)
Onion (kanda/pyaz)
ingredients.householdMeasure: ½ medium onion, finely chopped (about ⅓ cup)

equipment: Kadai or wide frying pan with a lid
Measuring spoons and a measuring cup (a regular tea cup and teaspoons work as a stand-in)

steps.title: Measure the poha
steps.text: Put 60 g (¾ cup) thick poha into the colander.
steps.tip: Pick out any husk or small stones you see.
steps.visualCue: Flakes are whole and not broken into dust.
steps.cameraCheck: The colander with ¾ cup of dry poha
steps.videoShot: The poha pouring from the cup into the colander.

steps.title: Rinse the poha
steps.text: Hold the colander under running tap water and gently turn the flakes with your fingers so all of them get wet.
steps.tip: Do not soak the poha in a bowl of water. That is the main reason poha turns mushy.
steps.visualCue: Every flake looks wet and a shade brighter. The water running off is mostly clear.
steps.cameraCheck: The wet poha in the colander
steps.videoShot: Water running over the poha while fingers turn it.

steps.title: Drain the poha
steps.text: Shake the colander 2–3 times and leave it over a bowl to drain.
steps.visualCue: No water is dripping out any more.
steps.cameraCheck: The colander resting over the bowl
steps.videoShot: The colander being shaken and set down.

steps.title: Season and rest the poha
steps.text: Sprinkle 1.5 g (¼ tsp) salt, 2 g (½ tsp) sugar and 0.5 g (⅛ tsp) turmeric over the damp poha. Toss gently with your fingertips, then leave it to rest.
steps.tip: Adding the turmeric now, not in the pan, gives an even colour without stirring the poha too much later.
steps.visualCue: The flakes turn an even pale yellow.
steps.cameraCheck: The yellow poha in the colander
steps.videoShot: The spices sprinkling over the poha, then a gentle toss.

steps.title: Chop the onion
steps.text: Finely chop 60 g (½ medium) onion.
steps.visualCue: Small, even pieces about the size of a grain of rice or a lentil.
steps.cameraCheck: ⅓ cup of chopped onion on the board
steps.videoShot: The knife chopping the onion into small dice.

steps.title: Chop the chilli
steps.text: Slit 1 green chilli (5 g) and cut it into small pieces.
steps.tip: Want it less hot? Remove the seeds first.
steps.visualCue: Thin rings or small bits
steps.cameraCheck: The chopped chilli on the board
steps.videoShot: The knife cutting the chilli.

steps.title: Prepare the herbs
steps.text: Wash 6–8 curry leaves and pat them dry. Chop 5 g (1 tbsp) coriander leaves.
steps.visualCue: The curry leaves are dry, so they won't splutter.
steps.cameraCheck: The curry leaves and chopped coriander side by side
steps.videoShot: The coriander being chopped.

steps.title: Cut the lemon
steps.text: Cut ¼ of a lemon and keep it ready.
steps.visualCue: A juicy wedge
steps.cameraCheck: The lemon wedge
steps.videoShot: The knife cutting the lemon wedge.

steps.title: Heat the oil
steps.text: Put the kadai on medium heat and add 10 ml (2 tsp) oil.
steps.visualCue: The oil shimmers and flows easily when you tilt the pan.
steps.cameraCheck: The kadai with oil
steps.videoShot: The oil swirling in the pan.

steps.title: Fry the peanuts
steps.text: Add 10 g (1 tbsp) peanuts and stir.
steps.tip: Take them out with a spoon and set aside if you want them extra crunchy. Otherwise leave them in.
steps.visualCue: The skins darken a little, the peanuts smell nutty and turn crunchy.
steps.cameraCheck: Golden peanuts in the pan
steps.videoShot: The peanuts being stirred in the oil.

steps.title: Add the mustard seeds
steps.text: Add 1 g (¼ tsp) mustard seeds.
steps.visualCue: The seeds crackle and pop.
steps.cameraCheck: Popping seeds in the pan
steps.videoShot: The mustard seeds spluttering.

steps.title: Add the cumin
steps.text: Add 0.5 g (⅛ tsp) cumin seeds (optional).
steps.visualCue: The cumin sizzles and darkens slightly.
steps.cameraCheck: The pan
steps.videoShot: The cumin sizzling.

steps.title: Add the curry leaves and chilli
steps.text: Add the curry leaves and green chilli.
steps.tip: Stand back. Wet leaves splutter hard.
steps.visualCue: A loud splutter, then the leaves turn crisp and glossy.
steps.cameraCheck: The leaves and chilli in the oil
steps.videoShot: The leaves hitting the oil.

steps.title: Sauté the onion
steps.text: Add the chopped onion and stir.
steps.visualCue: The onion turns soft and translucent, not brown.
steps.cameraCheck: The soft onions in the pan
steps.videoShot: The onions being stirred.

steps.title: Check the poha
steps.text: Press a flake between your fingers.
steps.visualCue: It squashes easily but holds its shape and is not pasty. If it still feels hard, sprinkle 1 tbsp water over it and wait 2 min.
steps.cameraCheck: A flake pressed between your fingers
steps.videoShot: Fingers pressing a flake.

steps.title: Add the poha
steps.text: Turn the heat to low and add the rested poha to the pan.
steps.visualCue: A yellow pile sitting over the onions
steps.cameraCheck: The pan with the poha added
steps.videoShot: The poha sliding into the pan.

steps.title: Mix the poha
steps.text: Fold gently from the bottom with the spatula until the onions and peanuts spread through it.
steps.tip: Lift and fold. Do not press or mash.
steps.visualCue: Even yellow colour with no white patches. The flakes are still separate.
steps.cameraCheck: The mixed poha
steps.videoShot: The spatula gently folding the poha.

steps.title: Steam the poha
steps.text: Cover with the lid and cook on low heat.
steps.visualCue: Steam on the inside of the lid, and the poha looks soft and fluffy when you open it.
steps.cameraCheck: The covered pan
steps.videoShot: The lid going on, then coming off to show steam.

steps.title: Add the lemon
steps.text: Switch off the heat. Squeeze 5 ml (1 tsp) lemon juice over the poha.
steps.tip: Add lemon only after the heat is off. Cooked lemon turns bitter.
steps.visualCue: The juice is spread over the top.
steps.cameraCheck: The lemon being squeezed over the pan
steps.videoShot: Lemon juice dripping over the poha.

steps.title: Add the coriander
steps.text: Scatter the chopped coriander over the poha and give it one last gentle fold.
steps.visualCue: Bright green flecks over yellow poha
steps.cameraCheck: The finished poha in the pan
steps.videoShot: The coriander falling onto the poha, then one fold.

steps.title: Plate the poha
steps.text: Spoon it onto a plate.
steps.visualCue: Fluffy, separate, yellow flakes with green herbs and brown peanuts
steps.cameraCheck: The served plate
steps.videoShot: A slow pan across the finished plate.

reasons: the home version uses only 2 tsp oil, no deep frying and very little sugar. It gets some protein and healthy fat from the peanuts and vegetables from the onion and herbs. It is still mostly refined carbohydrate with modest protein (about 8 g) and fibre (about 3 g). Restaurant versions usually use more oil, more sugar and a sev topping, which is deep-fried, so they are less healthy.

researchRating.basis: poha is one of India's most-loved everyday breakfasts. It is described as a "must" in eateries and a staple across Mumbai, and recipe pages get very high scores (for example, Indian Healthy Recipes: 5 stars from 301 votes; Cubes N Juliennes: 4.87 from 15 votes). Points are deducted because many people see it as plain, everyday food, and its texture often goes wrong (mushy or dry), a common complaint.

storage: Can go in the fridge for up to 1 day in an airtight box (it dries out and hardens after that). Freezing is not recommended because the flakes go crumbly. To reheat, sprinkle 1–2 tsp water, cover, and heat on low in a pan for 2–3 min, or microwave covered for 45–60 sec. Add fresh lemon after reheating.
leftoverRemix: Poha cutlets. Mash the leftover poha with 1 boiled potato, 1 tbsp besan and a pinch of chaat masala. Shape into small patties and shallow-fry on a tawa with 1 tsp oil until crisp, about 3 min per side. Serve with green chutney.
burnOff: about 5.6 km of running (390 ÷ 70 kcal/km, for a 70 kg adult), or about 7.8 km of brisk walking (about 1 hr 35 min at 5 km/h, using about 50 kcal/km for walking) (est.).
